040/**
041 * Provides String based properties like {@link System#getProperty(String)} for default
042 * configuration of logging levels and output. Since Rainbow Gum is configuration agnostic
043 * LogProperties is a simple string key and string value interface to allow almost any
044 * configuration implementation. The only required method to implement is
045 * {@link #valueOrNull(String)} and thus LogProperties is a functional like interface but
046 * using {@link LogProperties#builder()} is preferred so that a
047 * {@linkplain #description(String) description} can be added.
048 * <p>
049 * If a custom {@link LogProperties} is not configured the default RainbowGum uses System
050 * properties.
051 * <p>
052 * The built-in properties to configure RainbowGum are modeled after <a href=
053 * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/docs/3.1.0/reference/html/features.html#features.logging">
054 * Spring Boot logging </a>
055 * <p>
056 * LogProperties should generally be accessed with {@link #forKey(String)} (see
057 * {@link LogProperty}) which will allow safe <em>programmatic</em> data conversion of the
058 * flat key values and useful error messages to users if the property cannot be mapped or
059 * is missing. For more <em>declarative</em> injection of properties see
060 * {@link LogConfigurable} which will generate builders that can use LogProperties.
061 * <p>
062 * Rainbow Gum treats {@value #SEP} in the keys as special separator analogous to
063 * JavaScript/JSON and various other configuration systems. Furthermore to work with a
064 * wide set of configuration systems once a property key has a value it is
065 * <strong>RECOMMENDED</strong> that there should not be other property key value with a
066 * key that is a prefix of the previously mentioned key. For example allowing two
067 * properties <code>logging.example=stuff</code>, <code>logging.example.a=A</code> is not
068 * recommended as <code>logging.example</code> is defined as a leaf. The exception to this
069 * rule is logging levels mapped to logger names for consistency with Spring Boot.
070 * <p>
071 * Rainbow Gum out of the the box supports parsing two formats into properties:
072 * {@link Properties} text, and {@link URI#getRawQuery()} percent encoded query
073 * parameters. The two different formats have different behavior for
074 * {@link #listOrNull(String)} and {@link #mapOrNull(String)}. If a custom format of
075 * LogProperties is created those two methods may need to be extended.
076 * <p>
077 * A convention used through out Rainbow Gum is to have the property names as constants as
078 * it makes documentation easier. These constants name are suffixed with
079 * <code>_PROPERTY</code> or <code>_PREFIX</code> the former being a fully qualified key
080 * that maybe parameterized and the latter being a partial key ending with
081 * "<code>.</code>". The fully qualified keys are like leaves on a tree.
082 * <p>
083 * Property keys can be parameterized by using
084 * {@link LogProperties#interpolateKey(String, Map)} and a general pattern is
085 * <code>logging.component.{name}.prop</code> where {@value #NAME} is a parameter. Many
086 * property constants use this to allow multiple configuration of components by name.
087 *
088 * <table class="table">
089 * <caption><strong>Built-in Property Patterns</strong></caption>
090 * <tr>
091 * <th>Property Pattern</th>
092 * <th>Description</th>
093 * </tr>
094 * <tr>
095 * <td>{@value #LEVEL_PREFIX} + {@value #SEP} + logger = LEVEL</td>
096 * <td>Sets the level for the logger. If logger name is missing then it is considered the
097 * root logger. {@link Level#INFO} is the default level for the root logger.</td>
098 * </tr>
099 * <tr>
100 * <td>{@value #CHANGE_PREFIX} + {@value #SEP} + logger = boolean |
101 * List&lt;{@link ChangeType}&gt;</td>
102 * <td>Allows runtime changing of levels for the logger. By design RainbowGum does not
103 * allow loggers to change levels once initialized. This configuration will allow the
104 * level to be changed for the logger and its children and by default is false as the
105 * built-in {@link LogProperties} is generally static (system properties).</td>
106 * </tr>
107 * <tr>
108 * <td>{@value #ROUTES_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
109 * <td>A comma separated list of routes that should be enabled. If not set
110 * {@value LogRouter.Router#DEFAULT_ROUTER_NAME } is the default.</td>
111 * </tr>
112 * <tr>
113 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
114 * <td>A comma separated list of appenders associated with the route. If not set
115 * {@value #APPENDERS_PROPERTY} is used.</td>
116 * </tr>
117 * <tr>
118 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY} = <code>URI</code></td>
119 * <td>Looks up a publisher by URI scheme using the {@link LogPublisherRegistry}. The
120 * publisher is then configured by properties with {@value #PUBLISHER_PREFIX}.</td>
121 * </tr>
122 * <tr>
123 * <td>{@value #APPENDERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
124 * <td>A comma separated list of appenders that should be enabled. If not set
125 * {@value LogAppender#CONSOLE_APPENDER_NAME} is the default.</td>
126 * </tr>
127 * <tr>
128 * <td>{@value #APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY } = <code>URI</code></td>
129 * <td>Looks up an output by URI scheme using the {@link LogOutputRegistry}. The output is
130 * then configured by properties with {@value #OUTPUT_PREFIX}.</td>
131 * </tr>
132 * <tr>
133 * <td>{@value #APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY } = <code>URI</code></td>
134 * <td>Looks up an encoder by URI scheme using the {@link LogEncoderRegistry}. The encoder
135 * is then configured by properties with {@value #ENCODER_PREFIX}.</td>
136 * </tr>
137 * <tr>
138 * <tr>
139 * <td>{@value #OUTPUT_PREFIX} + <code>propertyName</code></td>
140 * <td>Configures the named output. The name of the output usually comes from the
141 * appender.</td>
142 * </tr>
143 * <tr>
144 * <td>{@value #ENCODER_PREFIX} + <code>propertyName</code></td>
145 * <td>Configures the named encoder. The name of the encoder usually comes from the
146 * appender.</td>
147 * </tr>
148 * <tr>
149 * <td>{@value #FILE_PROPERTY} = URI</td>
150 * <td>A URI or file path to log to a file. This is for Spring Boot compatibility.</td>
151 * </tr>
152 * </table>
153 *
154 * @see LogConfigurable
155 */
156public interface LogProperties {
157
158        /**
159         * properties separator.
160         */
161        static final String SEP = ".";
162
163        /**
164         * Logging properties prefix.
165         */
166        static final String ROOT_PREFIX = "logging" + SEP;
167
168        /**
169         * Controls direct fail-safe bootstrap diagnostics. {@code OFF} (also {@code false})
170         * is the default; {@code ERROR} dumps on build failure, while {@code INFO} also dumps
171         * after successful config builds. {@code ALL} (also {@code true}) additionally prints
172         * a {@link LogReporter} report after {@link RainbowGum#start()} starts the logging
173         * components. Read from system properties before properties providers run, so it
174         * remains available when loading configuration fails. The system property overrides
175         * {@link LogConfig.Builder#debug(LogConfig.DebugModeType)}.
176         */
177        static final String DEBUG_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "debug";
178
179        /**
180         * Logging level properties prefix. The value should be the name of a
181         * {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level level}.
182         */
183        static final String LEVEL_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "level";
184
185        /**
186         * Enabled level groups. The value should be a list of group names used on
187         * {@link #GROUP_PROPERTY}. This is to enable <a href=
188         * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.3.2/reference/features/logging.html#features.logging.log-groups">
189         * Spring Boot like Log Groups </a>. <em>Note that unlike Spring Boot groups are not
190         * enabled unless this property contains the group.</em>
191         */
192        static final String GROUPS_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "groups";
193
194        /**
195         * Group property with list of logger names. The level of the group is set with
196         * <code>{@value #LEVEL_PREFIX} + .{name} = Level</code> or on the router itself with
197         * <code>{@value #ROUTE_LEVEL_PREFIX} + .{name} = Level</code>. This is largely
198         * compatible with <a href=
199         * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.3.2/reference/features/logging.html#features.logging.log-groups">
200         * Spring Boot Log Groups </a>.
201         * @see LevelResolver#parseLevel(String)
202         */
203        static final String GROUP_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "group.{name}";
204
205        /**
206         * Logging change configuration allowed property.
207         */
208        static final String GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.change";
209
210        /**
211         * The level threshold of events captured before Rainbow Gum is fully bound. Before
212         * Rainbow Gum is bound events are queued. By default events that are below
213         * <code>INFO</code> are not queued.
214         */
215        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_LEVEL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.level";
216
217        /**
218         * The level threshold of queued events reported to standard error before Rainbow Gum
219         * is bound. Defaults to <code>ERROR</code>.
220         */
221        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_ERROR_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.error";
222
223        /**
224         * Will globally turn of any ANSI escape output as well disable extensions that do
225         * things for ANSI escape like JANSI. If not set this is derived automatically from
226         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.AnsiSupport#isAnsiSupported()} which checks
227         * whether the process is attached to an ANSI capable terminal.
228         */
229        static final String GLOBAL_ANSI_DISABLE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.ansi.disable";
230
231        /**
232         * If true guarantees no appender will use {@code synchronized} for its locking,
233         * regardless of an explicitly requested
234         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}: an explicit
235         * request for that type is downgraded to
236         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} instead of being honored.
237         * Intended for deployments that want a hard guarantee independent of per-appender
238         * configuration - e.g. still running JDK versions before
239         * <a href="https://openjdk.org/jeps/491">JEP 491</a> (JDK 24), where
240         * {@code synchronized} pins the carrier platform thread when called from a virtual
241         * thread, and that would rather not rely on per-appender configuration to avoid it.
242         */
243        static final String GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.appender.reentrantLock";
244
245        /**
246         * A global, process-wide guarantee of no {@link ThreadLocal} anywhere in the logging
247         * path, for deployments that want that guaranteed independent of
248         * per-appender/per-module configuration. When active:
249         * <ul>
250         * <li>Any appender that would otherwise use
251         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} or
252         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} (the default,
253         * plus its {@code synchronized}-locking sibling - both {@link ThreadLocal}-backed) is
254         * downgraded to {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_NEW_BUFFER} instead - an
255         * explicit request for {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#REUSE_BUFFER} (already
256         * {@link ThreadLocal}-free) is left as-is rather than also forced to
257         * {@code LOCK_NEW_BUFFER}.</li>
258         * <li>{@code rainbowgum-slf4j}'s MDC support is disabled, the same as an explicit
259         * {@code logging.mdc.type=NOOP} - see {@code RainbowGumSLF4JServiceProvider}.</li>
260         * </ul>
261         * @apiNote unlike {@link #GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY} this reaches
262         * beyond {@code core} into {@code rainbowgum-slf4j} - both independently read this
263         * same property key rather than one module exposing a shared static flag the other
264         * consumes, since there is no other cross-module wiring between them today.
265         */
266        static final String GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.threadlocalDisabled";
267
268        /**
269         * Opts every appender/encoder that has not been given an explicit choice into
270         * whatever this release currently believes is the best buffering/locking strategy for
271         * the platform the process is actually running on, instead of the fixed defaults
272         * ({@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}, a
273         * {@link java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder}-based encode) used otherwise. An explicit
274         * choice - programmatic ({@code appenderType(...)}, {@code useGetBytes(...)}) or via
275         * a more specific property ({@link LogAppender#APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY}) - always wins
276         * over this property; it only ever fills in what would otherwise be unset.
277         * <p>
278         * <strong>What "best" resolves to today, and why that is not a contract:</strong>
279         * currently this only has an effect under GraalVM native-image (detected the same way
280         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#AUTO_DETECT} is - see its javadoc), where it sets
281         * the default appender type to {@code AUTO_DETECT} (this benchmark's own measurements
282         * found {@code SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} a real, repeatable win over the
283         * plain-JVM default there) and defaults text encoders to
284         * {@code String.getBytes(Charset)}-based encoding over the default
285         * {@code CharsetEncoder}-based one. On a plain JVM this property currently changes
286         * nothing at all - the measurements that motivated the native-image behavior above
287         * pointed the other way on HotSpot. None of this is a promise: as this project
288         * benchmarks more platforms, JDK versions, and encode strategies, what "optimize"
289         * resolves to on a given platform - including whether it does anything on a plain JVM
290         * at all - can and will change between releases without notice. Pin an explicit
291         * appender type/encoder strategy instead if a deployment needs a specific one to
292         * always be used.
293         */
294        static final String GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.optimize";
295
296        /**
297         * Maximum number of alerts {@link LogAlerts} holds in its ring buffer. Read once,
298         * from whatever {@link LogProperties} {@link LogConfig.Builder#build()} has already
299         * resolved by the time it constructs {@link LogAlerts} - before any
300         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} runs.
301         * @see LogAlerts#DEFAULT_CAPACITY
302         */
303        static final String ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.capacity";
304
305        /**
306         * What {@link LogAlerts} does, once on {@link LogLifecycle#start(LogConfig) start},
307         * if it has recorded at least one error alert and still has zero
308         * {@link LogAlerts.Listener}s registered - see
309         * {@link LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction} for the three choices and
310         * {@link LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction#DUMP} for the default.
311         */
312        static final String ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.unobservedErrorsAction";
313
314        /**
315         * Logging change properties prefix.
316         */
317        static final String CHANGE_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "change";
318
319        /**
320         * Logging caller info properties prefix. Independent of {@link #CHANGE_PREFIX} -
321         * resolved through its own logger-name hierarchy walk, so a value here can never be
322         * silently overridden by a more specific {@link #CHANGE_PREFIX} entry or vice versa.
323         */
324        static final String CALLER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "caller";
325
326        /**
327         * Logging file property for default single file appending. The value should be a URI.
328         */
329        static final String FILE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "file.name";
330
331        /**
332         * A common key parameter is called name.
333         */
334        static final String NAME = "name";
335
336        /**
337         * For properties keys that are parameterized with {@value #NAME} the name often used
338         * if not specified is: {@value #DEFAULT_NAME}.
339         */
340        static final String DEFAULT_NAME = "default";
341
342        /**
343         * Logging output prefix for configuration.
344         */
345        static final String OUTPUT_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "output.{" + NAME + "}.";
346
347        /**
348         * Logging output prefix for configuration.
349         */
350        static final String ENCODER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "encoder.{" + NAME + "}.";
351
352        /**
353         * Enabled Logging appenders. The value should be a list of names. This is equivalent
354         * to {@value #ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY} with name "default".
355         */
356        static final String APPENDERS_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "appenders";
357
358        /**
359         * Logging appender prefix for configuration.
360         */
361        static final String APPENDER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "appender.{" + NAME + "}.";
362
363        /**
364         * Output appender property.
365         */
366        static final String APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_PREFIX + "output";
367
368        /**
369         * Encoder appender property.
370         */
371        static final String APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_PREFIX + "encoder";
372
373        /**
374         * Appender flags. A list of flags (usually comma separated).
375         * @see AppenderFlag
376         */
377        static final String APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_PREFIX + "flags";
378
379        /**
380         * Appender type (buffer/locking strategy). Unlike {@value #APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY}
381         * this is a single value, not a list.
382         * @see LogAppender.AppenderType
383         */
384        static final String APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_PREFIX + "type";
385
386        /**
387         * Logging publisher prefix for configuration.
388         */
389        static final String PUBLISHER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "publisher.{" + NAME + "}.";
390
391        /**
392         * Routes enabled with names comma separated.
393         */
394        static final String ROUTES_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "routes";
395
396        /**
397         * Route prefix for configuration.
398         */
399        static final String ROUTE_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "route.{" + NAME + "}.";
400
401        /**
402         * Logging publisher URI property.
403         */
404        static final String ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY = ROUTE_PREFIX + "publisher";
405
406        /**
407         * Appenders associated with a route comma separated.
408         */
409        static final String ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY = ROUTE_PREFIX + "appenders";
410
411        /**
412         * Logging level properties prefix. The value should be the name of a
413         * {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level level}.
414         */
415        static final String ROUTE_LEVEL_PREFIX = ROUTE_PREFIX + "level";
416
417        /**
418         * Route flags.
419         */
420        static final String ROUTE_FLAGS_PROPERTY = ROUTE_PREFIX + "flags";
421
422        /**
423         * Analogous to {@link System#getProperty(String)}.
424         * @param key property name.
425         * @return property value.
426         */
427        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key);
428
429        /**
430         * Analogous to {@link System#getProperty(String, String)} with the exception that the
431         * fallback cannot be null and the return cannot be null.
432         * @param key property name.
433         * @param fallback returned if the value is not found and may not be null.
434         * @return value found or fallback.
435         */
436        default String value(String key, String fallback) {
437                Objects.requireNonNull(fallback);
438                String v = valueOrNull(key);
439                if (v != null) {
440                        return v;
441                }
442                return fallback;
443        }
444
445        /**
446         * Gets a list or null if the key is missing and by default uses
447         * {@link #parseList(String)}. The default implementation will parse the string value
448         * as a list using {@link LogProperties#parseList(String)} but custom implementations
449         * may rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing
450         * configuration system.
451         * <p>
452         * The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated
453         * and percent-encoded (<a href=
454         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
455         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded</a>) for entries needing to contain the separator
456         * or an equals sign, for example: <pre><code>
457         * logging.appenders=console,file
458         * </code></pre> resolves to <code>["console", "file"]</code>, and: <pre><code>
459         * logging.appenders=one%20two,three%2Cfour
460         * </code></pre> (a space and an escaped comma) resolves to
461         * <code>["one two", "three,four"]</code>.
462         * @param key property name.
463         * @return list or <code>null</code>.
464         * @apiNote the reason empty list is not returned for missing key is that it creates
465         * ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.
466         */
467        default @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
468                String s = valueOrNull(key);
469                if (s == null) {
470                        return null;
471                }
472                return parseList(s);
473        }
474
475        /**
476         * Gets a map or null if the key is missing and by default uses
477         * {@link #parseMap(String)}. The default implementation will parse the string value
478         * as map using {@link LogProperties#parseMap(String)} but custom implementations may
479         * rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing configuration
480         * system.
481         * <p>
482         * The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated
483         * <code>key=value</code> pairs, percent-encoded (<a href=
484         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
485         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded</a>) for entries needing to contain the separator
486         * or an equals sign, for example: <pre><code>
487         * logging.encoder.gelf.headers=environment=prod,region=us-east
488         * </code></pre> resolves to
489         * <code>{"environment": "prod", "region": "us-east"}</code>, and: <pre><code>
490         * logging.encoder.gelf.headers=region=us%20east
491         * </code></pre> (a percent-encoded space) resolves to
492         * <code>{"region": "us east"}</code>.
493         * @param key property name.
494         * @return map or <code>null</code>.
495         * @apiNote the reason empty map is not returned for missing key is that it creates
496         * ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.
497         */
498        default @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
499                String s = valueOrNull(key);
500                if (s == null) {
501                        return null;
502                }
503                return parseMap(s);
504        }
505
506        /**
507         * Visits this properties with visitor, by default just applying visitor to this and
508         * key directly. A composite/aggregate {@link LogProperties} (one backed by more than
509         * one underlying source) overrides this to recursively visit each of its members in
510         * order, returning the first non-<code>null</code> result - which member actually
511         * produced it is exactly what visitor is handed as its first argument, so a composite
512         * never needs to know anything about what visitor is trying to build (a raw value, a
513         * resolved property, or anything else); it just walks its members and stops at the
514         * first hit.
515         * @param <R> result type.
516         * @param key property key.
517         * @param visitor applied to (the member of this properties that ends up handling the
518         * visit, key); a <code>null</code> return means keep visiting.
519         * @return first non-<code>null</code> result, or <code>null</code> if nothing visited
520         * produced one.
521         */
522        default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key,
523                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor) {
524                return visitor.apply(this, key);
525        }
526
527        /**
528         * Searches up a {@value #SEP} separated path using this properties to check for
529         * values. The first value not missing (not <code>null</code>) will be returned.
530         * @param <T> result type
531         * @param root prefix.
532         * @param key partial key that will have prefix concated on each try of func.
533         * @param func convert function where <code>null</code> return means to keep
534         * searching.
535         * @return closest value or <code>null</code> if no value can be found.
536         * @see #findUpPathOrNull(String, Function)
537         */
538        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
539        default <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findOrNull(String root, String key,
540                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable T> func) {
541                return findUpPathOrNull(key, k -> func.apply(this, concatKey(root, k)));
542        }
543
544        /**
545         * Starts resolving a property under key against this properties - the preferred entry
546         * point for looking up and converting a property, see {@link LogProperty}.
547         * @param key key, must start with {@value #ROOT_PREFIX} and not start or end with
548         * {@value #SEP}.
549         * @return a LogProperty ready to be resolved (e.g. via
550         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()}) or given fallback keys to try (via
551         * {@link LogProperty#or(String)}).
552         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if key is malformed.
553         */
554        default LogProperty forKey(String key) {
555                return LogProperty.of(this, key);
556        }
557
558        /**
559         * Starts resolving a property under key, with a <code>{name}</code> placeholder in
560         * key interpolated to nameParam, against this properties.
561         * @param key key, containing a <code>{name}</code> placeholder, and once interpolated
562         * must start with {@value #ROOT_PREFIX} and not start or end with {@value #SEP}.
563         * @param nameParam value to interpolate for <code>{name}</code> in key.
564         * @return a LogProperty ready to be resolved (e.g. via
565         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()}) or given fallback keys to try (via
566         * {@link LogProperty#or(String, String)}).
567         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the interpolated key is malformed.
568         */
569        default LogProperty forKey(String key, String nameParam) {
570                return LogProperty.of(this, key, nameParam);
571        }
572
573        /**
574         * Describes a key and by default is usually just the key.
575         * @param key key.
576         * @return usually the key.
577         */
578        default String description(String key) {
579                return key;
580        }
581
582        /**
583         * When log properties are coalesced this method is used to resolve order. A higher
584         * number gives higher precedence.
585         * @return zero by default.
586         */
587        default int order() {
588                return 0;
589        }

591        /**
592         * Abstract log properties builder.
593         *
594         * @param <T> builder.
595         * @apiNote this abstract class can largely be ignored hence why it is sealed.
596         */
597        public sealed abstract class AbstractBuilder<T> {
598
599                /**
600                 * description
601                 */
602                protected @Nullable String description = null;
603
604                /**
605                 * order
606                 */
607                protected int order = 0;
608
609                /**
610                 * rename key
611                 */
612                protected Function<String, String> renameKey = s -> s;
613
614                /**
615                 * fallbacks
616                 */
617                protected List<LogProperties> fallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
618
619                /**
620                 * Ignored.
621                 */
622                protected AbstractBuilder() {
623                }
624
625                /**
626                 * Add a fallback properties.
627                 * @param properties fallback not null.
628                 * @return this.
629                 */
630                public T with(LogProperties properties) {
631                        this.fallbacks.add(properties);
632                        return self();
633                }
634
635                /**
636                 * For returning this.
637                 * @return this builder.
638                 */
639                protected abstract T self();
640
641                /**
642                 * Description for properties.
643                 * @param description not null.
644                 * @return this.
645                 */
646                public T description(String description) {
647                        this.description = description;
648                        return self();
649                }
650
651                /**
652                 * When log properties are coalesced this method is used to resolve order. A
653                 * higher number gives higher precedence.
654                 * @param order order.
655                 * @return this.
656                 */
657                public T order(int order) {
658                        this.order = order;
659                        return self();
660                }
661
662                /**
663                 * Renames the key before it accesses function.
664                 * @param renameKey rename key function.
665                 * @return this.
666                 */
667                public T renameKey(Function<String, String> renameKey) {
668                        this.renameKey = renameKey;
669                        return self();
670                }
671
672                /**
673                 * Removes the prefix from a key before it accesses the underlying properties.
674                 * @param prefix to be removed from start of key.
675                 * @return this.
676                 */
677                public T removeKeyPrefix(String prefix) {
678                        return renameKey(k -> LogProperties.removeKeyPrefix(k, prefix));
679                }
680
681        }

683        /**
684         * Builder for properties.
685         */
686        public final static class Builder extends AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
687
688                private @Nullable Function<Builder, LogProperties> provider = null;
689
690                private Builder() {
691                }
692
693                @Override
694                protected Builder self() {
695                        return this;
696                }
697
698                private Builder provider(Function<Builder, LogProperties> provider) {
699                        if (this.provider != null) {
700                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("from already set");
701                        }
702                        this.provider = provider;
703                        return this;
704                }
705
706                /**
707                 * Sets what is called on {@link LogProperties#valueOrNull(String)}.
708                 * @param function valueOrNull func.
709                 * @return this.
710                 */
711                public Builder fromFunction(@SuppressWarnings("exports") Function<String, @Nullable String> function) {
712                        return provider((b) -> new DefaultLogProperties(function,
713                                        Objects.requireNonNullElse(description, "function"), renameKey, order));
714                }
715
716                /**
717                 * Parses a string as {@link Properties}.
718                 * <p>
719                 * The parameter is the <strong>contents</strong> of a properties file, not a
720                 * resource, path, or file name. Passing a name such as
721                 * {@code "logging.properties"} does not load that file; it is parsed as a single
722                 * key with an empty value.
723                 * @param properties properties content as a string, for example
724                 * {@code "logging.level=INFO"}.
725                 * @return this.
726                 * @apiNote Rainbow Gum core does not read resources from the filesystem or the
727                 * classpath. If external properties are needed, it is the caller's responsibility
728                 * to read them into a string (or use a module that does, like
729                 * {@code rainbowgum-simple-props}).
730                 */
731                public Builder fromProperties(String properties) {
732                        if (description == null) {
733                                description = "PROPERTIES_STRING";
734                        }
735                        return fromFunction(PropertiesParser.readProperties(properties)::get);
736                }
737
738                /**
739                 * Parses a string as a URI query string. If the URI has no query portion then it
740                 * will be equivalent to empty properties.
741                 * @param uri percent encoded uri with separator as "<code>&amp;</code>" and key
742                 * value separator of "<code>=</code>".
743                 * @return this.
744                 */
745                public Builder fromURIQuery(URI uri) {
746                        String query = uri.getRawQuery();
747                        return provider((b) -> queryToProperties(query,
748                                        Objects.requireNonNullElse(description, "URI_QUERY(" + LogRedactor.redactUri(uri) + ")")));
749                }
750
751                private MultiMapProperties queryToProperties(@Nullable String query, String description) {
752                        Map<String, List<String>> multiMap;
753                        if (query == null) {
754                                multiMap = Map.of();
755                        }
756                        else {
757                                multiMap = parseMultiMap(query);
758                        }
759                        var properties = new MultiMapProperties(multiMap, description, renameKey, order);
760                        return properties;
761                }
762
763                /**
764                 * Builds LogProperties based on builder config.
765                 * @return this.
766                 */
767                public LogProperties build() {
768                        var f = this.provider;
769                        if (f == null) {
770                                if (!fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
771                                        return LogProperties.of(fallbacks);
772                                }
773                                throw new IllegalStateException("from was not set");
774                        }
775
776                        var first = f.apply(this);
777                        if (fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
778                                return first;
779                        }
780                        List<LogProperties> combined = new ArrayList<>();
781                        combined.add(first);
782                        combined.addAll(fallbacks);
783                        return LogProperties.of(combined);
784                }
785
786                static abstract class AbstractLogProperties implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
787
788                        protected final String description;
789
790                        protected final Function<String, String> renameKey;
791
792                        protected final int order;
793
794                        public AbstractLogProperties(String description, Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
795                                super();
796                                this.description = description;
797                                this.renameKey = renameKey;
798                                this.order = order;
799                        }
800
801                        @Override
802                        public int order() {
803                                return this.order;
804                        }
805
806                        @Override
807                        public String description(String key) {
808                                String rename = renameKey.apply(key);
809                                return descriptionForKey(description, rename);
810                        }
811
812                        @Override
813                        public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
814                                out.append(description);
815                        }
816
817                        @Override
818                        public String toString() {
819                                return getClass().getSimpleName() + "[description='" + description + "', " + "order=" + order + "]";
820                        }
821
822                }
823
824                private static final class DefaultLogProperties extends AbstractLogProperties {
825
826                        private final Function<String, @Nullable String> func;
827
828                        DefaultLogProperties(Function<String, @Nullable String> func, String description,
829                                        Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
830                                super(description, renameKey, order);
831                                this.func = func;
832                        }
833
834                        @Override
835                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
836                                return func.apply(renameKey.apply(key));
837                        }
838
839                }
840
841        }

843        /**
844         * A log properties that can be mutated like a map.
845         */
846        public interface MutableLogProperties extends LogProperties {
847
848                /**
849                 * Assigns key to a value.
850                 * @param key key.
851                 * @param value value if null will remove the key.
852                 * @return this.
853                 */
854                MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value);
855
856                /**
857                 * Builder for MutableLogProperties.
858                 * @return builder.
859                 */
860                public static Builder builder() {
861                        return new Builder();
862                }
863
864                /**
865                 * Mutable Log properties builder.
866                 */
867                public final class Builder extends AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
868
869                        private Map<String, String> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
870
871                        private Builder() {
872                        }
873
874                        @Override
875                        protected Builder self() {
876                                return this;
877                        }
878
879                        /**
880                         * Sets the backing mutable map.
881                         * @param map backing map.
882                         * @return this.
883                         */
884                        public Builder with(Map<String, String> map) {
885                                this.map = map;
886                                return this;
887                        }
888
889                        /**
890                         * Parses a string as {@link Properties} useful for unit testing with Java
891                         * multiline string literal.
892                         * @param properties properties as a string.
893                         * @return this.
894                         */
895                        public Builder copyProperties(String properties) {
896                                map.putAll(PropertiesParser.readProperties(properties));
897                                return this;
898                        }
899
900                        /**
901                         * Builds a mutable log properties.
902                         * @return mutable log properties.
903                         */
904                        public MutableLogProperties build() {
905                                String description = this.description;
906                                if (description == null) {
907                                        description = "custom mutable";
908                                }
909                                var first = new MapLogProperties(map, description, renameKey, order);
910                                if (fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
911                                        return first;
912                                }
913                                List<LogProperties> combined = new ArrayList<>();
914                                combined.add(first);
915                                combined.addAll(fallbacks);
916                                return new CompositeMutableLogProperties(sort(combined));
917                        }
918
919                        private static final class MapLogProperties extends LogProperties.Builder.AbstractLogProperties
920                                        implements MutableLogProperties {
921
922                                private final Map<String, String> map;
923
924                                MapLogProperties(Map<String, String> map, String description, Function<String, String> renameKey,
925                                                int order) {
926                                        super(description, renameKey, order);
927                                        this.map = map;
928                                }
929
930                                @Override
931                                public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
932                                        return map.get(renameKey.apply(key));
933                                }
934
935                                @Override
936                                public MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value) {
937                                        Objects.requireNonNull(key);
938                                        key = renameKey.apply(key);
939                                        if (value == null) {
940                                                map.remove(key);
941                                                return this;
942                                        }
943                                        map.put(key, value);
944                                        return this;
945                                }
946
947                        }
948
949                }
950
951        }

953        /**
954         * LogProperties builder.

961        /**
962         * Finds global properties by checking the currently bound rainbow gum and if not set
963         * use system properties. <strong>This method should be used sparingly and is
964         * preferred that you get the properties through a config instance instead.</strong>
965         * @return currently bound properties or system properties.
966         * @apiNote the intention of this method is to be used for ServiceLoader singleton
967         * components and other systems that maybe bound prior to rainbow gum loading that
968         * need to determine if they should be enabled.
969         */
970        public static LogProperties findGlobalProperties() {
971                return findGlobalProperties(() -> StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES);
972        }
973
974        /**
975         * Finds global properties by checking the currently bound rainbow gum and if not set
976         * use the supplier as the fallback. <strong>This method should be used sparingly and
977         * is preferred that you get the properties through a config instance
978         * instead.</strong>
979         * @param fallback supplier to use if no rainbow gum is bound.
980         * @return currently bound properties or fallback.
981         * @apiNote the intention of this method is to be used for ServiceLoader singleton
982         * components and other systems that maybe bound prior to rainbow gum loading that
983         * need to determine if they should be enabled.
984         */
985        public static LogProperties findGlobalProperties(Supplier<? extends LogProperties> fallback) {
986                var gum = RainbowGum.getOrNull();
987                if (gum != null) {
988                        return gum.config().properties();
989                }
990                return Objects.requireNonNull(fallback.get());
991        }

993        /**
994         * Creates log properties from many log properties.
995         * @param logProperties list of properties.
996         * @param fallback if the logProperties list is empty.
997         * @return log properties
998         */
999        public static LogProperties of(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties, LogProperties fallback) {
1000                if (logProperties.isEmpty()) {
1001                        return fallback;
1002                }
1003                if (logProperties.size() == 1) {
1004                        return Objects.requireNonNull(logProperties.get(0));
1005                }
1006                var array = sort(logProperties);
1007                return new CompositeLogProperties(array);
1008        }
1009
1010        private static LogProperties[] sort(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties) {
1011                @SuppressWarnings("null") // TODO eclipse array issue
1012                LogProperties[] array = logProperties.stream()
1013                        .filter(p -> p != StandardProperties.EMPTY)
1014                        .toArray(size -> new LogProperties[size]);
1015                Arrays.sort(array, Comparator.comparingInt(LogProperties::order).reversed());
1016                return array;
1017        }

1019        /**
1020         * Creates log properties from many log properties.
1021         * @param logProperties the list of properties.
1022         * @return if the logProperties is empty {@link StandardProperties#EMPTY} will be
1023         * used.
1024         */
1025        public static LogProperties of(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties) {
1026                return of(logProperties, StandardProperties.EMPTY);
1027        }

1029        /**
1030         * Creates log properties from a URI query and provided properties. This is useful for
1031         * URI based providers where the URI query is contributing properties for the plugin.
1032         * @param uri query will be used to pull properties from using
1033         * {@link #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)}.
1034         * @param prefix part of the key that will stripped before accessing the URI
1035         * properties.
1036         * @param properties usually this is the properties coming from {@link LogConfig}.
1037         * @return combined properties where properties is tried first than the URI query
1038         * parameters.
1039         */
1040        public static LogProperties of(URI uri, String prefix, LogProperties properties) {
1041                return of(uri, prefix, properties, null);
1042        }
1043
1044        /**
1045         * Creates log properties from a URI query and provided properties. This is useful for
1046         * URI based providers where the URI query is contributing properties for the plugin.
1047         * @param uri query will be used to pull properties from using
1048         * {@link #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)}.
1049         * @param prefix part of the key that will stripped before accessing the URI
1050         * properties.
1051         * @param properties usually this is the properties coming from {@link LogConfig}.
1052         * @param uriKey where the URI came from.
1053         * @return combined properties where properties is tried first than the URI query
1054         * parameters.
1055         */
1056        public static LogProperties of(URI uri, String prefix, LogProperties properties, @Nullable String uriKey) {
1057                /*
1058                 * TODO this should be integrated with the whole providers and registries.
1059                 */
1060                String propDesc = uriKey != null ? "[" + uriKey + "]->" : "";
1061                String description = propDesc + "URI(" + LogRedactor.redactUri(uri) + ")";
1062                var uriProperties = LogProperties.builder()
1063                        .description(description)
1064                        .fromURIQuery(uri)
1065                        .renameKey(s -> LogProperties.removeKeyPrefix(s, prefix))
1066                        .build();
1067                return LogProperties.of(List.of(properties, uriProperties));
1068        }
1069
1070        /**
1071         * Parse a {@linkplain URI#getRawQuery() URI query} in <a href=
1072         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
1073         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded </a> format useful for parsing properties values
1074         * that have key values embedded in them. <strong>This parser unlike form encoding
1075         * uses <code>%20</code> for space as the data is coming from a URI.</strong>
1076         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1077         * @param consumer accept will be called for each entry and if key (left hand) does
1078         * not have a "<code>=</code>" following it the second parameter on the consumer
1079         * accept will be passed <code>null</code>.
1080         */
1081        public static void parseUriQuery(String query,
1082                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1083                parseUriQuery(query, true, consumer);
1084        }
1085
1086        /**
1087         * Parses a URI query formatted string to a Map.
1088         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1089         * @return decoded key values with last key winning over previous equal keys.
1090         * @see #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)
1091         */
1092        public static Map<String, String> parseMap(String query) {
1093                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1094                parseUriQuery(query, (k, v) -> {
1095                        if (v != null) {
1096                                m.put(k, v);
1097                        }
1098                });
1099                return m;
1100        }
1101
1102        /**
1103         * Parses a URI query for a multiple value map. The list values of the map maybe empty
1104         * if the query parameter does not have any values associated with it which would be
1105         * the case if there is a parameter (key) with no "<code>=</code>" following it. For
1106         * example the following would have three entries of <code>a,b,c</code> all with empty
1107         * list: <pre>
1108         * <code>
1109         * a&amp;b&amp;c&amp;
1110         * </code> </pre>
1111         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1112         * @return decoded key values with multiple keys grouped together in order found.
1113         * @see #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)
1114         */
1115        public static Map<String, List<String>> parseMultiMap(String query) {
1116                Map<String, List<String>> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1117                BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> f = (k, v) -> {
1118                        List<String> list = Objects.requireNonNull(m.computeIfAbsent(k, _k -> new ArrayList<String>()));
1119                        if (v != null) {
1120                                list.add(v);
1121                        }
1122                };
1123                parseUriQuery(query, f);
1124                return m;
1125        }
1126
1127        /**
1128         * Parses a list of strings from a string that is <a href=
1129         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
1130         * percent encoded for escaping (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)</a> where the
1131         * separator can be either "<code>&amp;</code>" or "<code>,</code>".
1132         * <p>
1133         * An example would be using ampersand: <pre><code>
1134         *  "a&amp;b%20B&amp;c" -> ["a","b B","c"]
1135         *  </code> </pre> and comma: <pre><code>
1136         *  "a,b,c" -> ["a","b","c"]
1137         *  </code> </pre>
1138         * @param query the comma or ampersand delimited string that is in URI query format.
1139         * @return list of strings
1140         */
1141        public static List<String> parseList(String query) {
1142                List<String> list = new ArrayList<>();
1143                parseUriQuery(query, (k, v) -> list.add(k));
1144                return list;
1145        }
1146
1147        private static void parseUriQuery(String query, boolean decode, BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1148                parseUriQuery(query, decode, "[&,]", consumer);
1149        }
1150
1151        private static void parseUriQuery(String query, boolean decode, String sep,
1152                        BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1153                /*
1154                 * TODO default java split has issues but is very fast
1155                 */
1156                @SuppressWarnings("StringSplitter")
1157                String[] pairs = query.split(sep);
1158                for (String pair : pairs) {
1159                        int idx = pair.indexOf("=");
1160                        String key;
1161                        String value;
1162                        if (idx == 0) {
1163                                continue;
1164                        }
1165                        else if (idx < 0) {
1166                                key = pair;
1167                                value = null;
1168                        }
1169                        else {
1170                                key = pair.substring(0, idx);
1171                                value = pair.substring(idx + 1);
1172                        }
1173                        if (decode) {
1174                                key = PercentCodec.decode(key, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1175                                if (value != null) {
1176                                        value = PercentCodec.decode(value, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1177                                }
1178
1179                        }
1180                        if (key.isBlank()) {
1181                                continue;
1182                        }
1183                        consumer.accept(key, value);
1184                }
1185        }
1186
1187        /**
1188         * Common static log properties such as System properties ane environment variables.
1189         */
1190        @CaseChanging
1191        enum StandardProperties implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
1192
1193                /**
1194                 * Empty properties. The order is <code>-1</code>.
1195                 */
1196                EMPTY {
1197                        @Override
1198                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1199                                return null;
1200                        }
1201
1202                        @Override
1203                        public int order() {
1204                                return -1;
1205                        }
1206                },
1207                /**
1208                 * Uses {@link System#getProperty(String)} for {@link #valueOrNull(String)}. The
1209                 * {@link #order()} is <code>400</code> which the same value as MicroProfile
1210                 * config ordinal.
1211                 */
1212                SYSTEM_PROPERTIES {
1213                        @Override
1214                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1215                                return System.getProperty(key);
1216                        }
1217
1218                        @Override
1219                        public int order() {
1220                                return 400;
1221                        }
1222                },
1223                /**
1224                 * Uses {@link System#getenv(String)} for {@link #valueOrNull(String)}.The
1225                 * {@link #order()} is <code>300</code> which is the same value as MicroProfile
1226                 * config ordinal.
1227                 */
1228                ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES {
1229                        @Override
1230                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1231                                return System.getenv(translateKey(key));
1232                        }
1233
1234                        @Override
1235                        protected String translateKey(String key) {
1236                                return key.replace(".", "_");
1237                        }
1238
1239                        @Override
1240                        public int order() {
1241                                return 300;
1242                        }
1243                };
1244
1245                @Override
1246                public String description(String key) {
1247                        String k = translateKey(key);
1248                        return name() + "[" + k + "]";
1249                }
1250
1251                /*
1252                 * Each constant's own per-constant class body (see EMPTY/SYSTEM_PROPERTIES/
1253                 * ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES above) makes getClass() an anonymous subclass with no
1254                 * canonical name, so without this LogPropertiesReporting's fallback chain would
1255                 * land on the description(dummyKey) branch instead: name() alone is a cleaner
1256                 * report for the single most common LogProperties in practice (the default when
1257                 * nothing else is configured).
1258                 */
1259                @Override
1260                public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
1261                        out.append(name());
1262                }
1263
1264                /**
1265                 * Translate the key.
1266                 * @param key input
1267                 * @return output
1268                 */
1269                protected String translateKey(String key) {
1270                        return key;
1271                }
1272
1273        }
1274
1275        /**
1276         * Searches a {@value LogProperties#SEP} separated property path recursing up the path
1277         * till a non null value (not missing) is found.
1278         * <p>
1279         * For example assume we have a single property set like
1280         * <code>logging.level.com.stuff=DEBUG</code> and we call this function with
1281         * <code>logging.level.com.stuff.a.b</code>.
1282         * <ol>
1283         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff.a.b</code> will resolve to <code>null</code></li>
1284         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff.a</code> will resolve to <code>null</code></li>
1285         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff</code> will resolve to <code>"DEBUG"</code>, stop
1286         * and return <code>"DEBUG"</code>.</li>
1287         * </ol>
1288         * @param <T> type to return.
1289         * @param key the initial path.
1290         * @param resolveFunc function that returns the value at path or <code>null</code>.
1291         * @return value or <code>null</code> if no non null value can be found.
1292         */
1293        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
1294        public static <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findUpPathOrNull(String key,
1295                        Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc) {
1296                return searchPath(key, resolveFunc, SEP);
1297        }
1298
1299        private static <T> @Nullable T searchPath(String key, Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc, String sep) {
1300                String tempName = key;
1301                @Nullable T level = null;
1302                int indexOfLastDot = tempName.length();
1303                while ((level == null) && (indexOfLastDot > -1)) {
1304                        tempName = tempName.substring(0, indexOfLastDot);
1305                        level = resolveFunc.apply(tempName);
1306                        indexOfLastDot = tempName.lastIndexOf(sep);
1307                }
1308                if (level != null) {
1309                        return level;
1310                }
1311                return resolveFunc.apply("");
1312        }
1313
1314        /**
1315         * Concats a key using {@link #SEP} to the root prefix.
1316         * @param name key.
1317         * @return concat key.
1318         */
1319        static String concatKey(String name) {
1320                return concatKey(LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX, name);
1321        }
1322
1323        /**
1324         * Concats a keys using {@link #SEP} as the separator.
1325         * @param prefix start of key.
1326         * @param name second part of key.
1327         * @return key.
1328         */
1329        static String concatKey(String prefix, String name) {
1330                if (name.equals("")) {
1331                        return prefix;
1332                }
1333                if (prefix.equals("")) {
1334                        return name;
1335                }
1336                if (prefix.endsWith(".")) {
1337                        prefix = prefix.substring(0, prefix.length() - 1);
1338                }
1339                if (name.startsWith(SEP)) {
1340                        return prefix + name;
1341                }
1342                return prefix + SEP + name;
1343        }
1344
1345        /**
1346         * Replace "{name}" tokens in property names.
1347         * @param key property name.
1348         * @param parameters tokens to replace with entry values.
1349         * @return interpolated property key.
1350         * @see #interpolateKey(String, Function)
1351         */
1352        static String interpolateKey(String key, Map<String, String> parameters) {
1353                return interpolateKey(key, parameters::get);
1354        }
1355
1356        /**
1357         * Replaces property <strong>key</strong> parameters by using the lookup function.
1358         * Property keys are often parameterized usually by some name. The parameters are
1359         * surrounded by curly braces and replaced by the lookup function. An example of the
1360         * format is <code>a.{PARAM}</code> which has a parameter named <code>PARAM</code>. If
1361         * the lookup function has <code>PARAM->b</code> then the result will be
1362         * <code>a.b</code>. If a value for a parameter is null (indicates not found) an
1363         * exception is thrown.
1364         * @param key to be interpolated.
1365         * @param lookup function that may return null for a parameter.
1366         * @return interpolated key with all parameters replaced.
1367         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the lookup function does not have a value for a
1368         * parameter.
1369         */
1370        public static String interpolateKey(String key,
1371                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") Function<String, ? extends @Nullable String> lookup)
1372                        throws IllegalArgumentException {
1373                var parameters = keyParameters(key);
1374                String result = key;
1375                for (String k : parameters) {
1376                        var v = lookup.apply(k);
1377                        if (v == null) {
1378                                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
1379                                                "Keyed parameter missing. key: '" + key + "' parameter: '" + k + "'");
1380                        }
1381                        LogProperty.Validator.validateKeyParameterValue(key, k, v);
1382                        result = result.replace("{" + k + "}", v);
1383                }
1384                return result;
1385        }
1386
1387        /**
1388         * Interpolates a named key which is a property key that has a {@value #NAME}.
1389         * @param key with name parameters.
1390         * @param name replace name token.
1391         * @return interpolated property key.
1392         */
1393        static String interpolateNamedKey(String key, String name) {
1394                return interpolateKey(key, Map.of(NAME, name));
1395        }
1396
1397        /**
1398         * Remove key prefix from the key. Prefix should end in "." but this method does not
1399         * check that.
1400         * @param key key whose prefix will be removed.
1401         * @param prefix property name prefix.
1402         * @return prefix removed if the string is prefixed.
1403         */
1404        static String removeKeyPrefix(String key, String prefix) {
1405                if (key.startsWith(prefix)) {
1406                        return key.substring(prefix.length());
1407                }
1408                return key;
1409        }
1410
1411        /**
1412         * Property prefix parameter pattern.
1413         */
1414        static final Pattern PARAMETER_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("\\{(.*?)\\}");
1415
1416        /**
1417         * Extract key parameters with {@link #PARAMETER_PATTERN}.
1418         * @param key also known as property name.
1419         * @return parameters in key.
1420         */
1421        static Set<String> keyParameters(String key) {
1422                Set<String> tokens = new LinkedHashSet<>();
1423                Matcher matcher = PARAMETER_PATTERN.matcher(key);
1424                while (matcher.find()) {
1425                        var t = matcher.group(1);
1426                        if (t == null) {
1427                                throw new IllegalStateException("bug with parameter pattern regex.");
1428                        }
1429                        tokens.add(t);
1430                }
1431                return tokens;
1432        }
1433
1434        /**
1435         * Validate key parameters.
1436         * @param key key to be interpolated with parameters.
1437         * @param parameters names of parameters which must <strong>equal</strong> the set of
1438         * the found parameters. while the order obviously does not matter the set cannot have
1439         * more parameters than found in the key.
1440         */
1441        static void validateKeyParameters(String key, Set<String> parameters) {
1442                var keyParameters = keyParameters(key);
1443                if (!parameters.equals(keyParameters)) {
1444                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Keyed parameter mismatch. key: '" + key + "' , key parameters: "
1445                                        + keyParameters + " provided parameters: " + parameters);
1446                }
1447        }
1448
1449        /**
1450         * Standard way to produce description for a key.
1451         * @param type the properties type name.
1452         * @param key the properties key translated.
1453         * @return description for key.
1454         */
1455        static String descriptionForKey(String type, String key) {
1456                return type + "[" + key + "]";
1457        }
1458
1459        /**
1460         * Standard way to produce description for a key found in a resource (a file or
1461         * similar), without a line number.
1462         * @param type the properties type name.
1463         * @param resource file like name.
1464         * @param key the properties key translated.
1465         * @return description for key.
1466         */
1467        static String descriptionForResource(String type, String resource, String key) {
1468                return type + "[" + resource + "][" + key + "]";
1469        }
1470
1471        /**
1472         * Standard way to produce description for a key found in a resource (a file or
1473         * similar) at a known index, usually a line number.
1474         * @param type the properties type name.
1475         * @param resource file like name.
1476         * @param key the properties key translated.
1477         * @param index usually line number of where key found.
1478         * @return description for key.
1479         */
1480        static String descriptionForResource(String type, String resource, String key, long index) {
1481                return type + "[" + resource + ":" + index + "][" + key + "]";
1482        }
1483
1484}

1486final class MultiMapProperties extends AbstractLogProperties {
1487
1488        private final Map<String, List<String>> multiMap;
1489
1490        public MultiMapProperties(Map<String, List<String>> multiMap, String description,
1491                        Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
1492                super(description, renameKey, order);
1493                this.multiMap = multiMap;
1494        }
1495
1496        @Override
1497        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1498                return _valueOrNull(renameKey.apply(key));
1499        }
1500
1501        private @Nullable String _valueOrNull(String key) {
1502                var list = multiMap.get(key);
1503                if (list == null || list.isEmpty()) {
1504                        return null;
1505                }
1506                return list.get(0);
1507        }
1508
1509        @Override
1510        public @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
1511                return multiMap.get(renameKey.apply(key));
1512        }
1513
1514        @Override
1515        public @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
1516                /*
1517                 * Now we check for dotted notation since key was not set. key.subkey=value
1518                 */
1519                String prefix = renameKey.apply(key) + LogProperties.SEP;
1520                LinkedHashMap<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1521                for (var k : multiMap.keySet()) {
1522                        if (k.startsWith(prefix) && !k.equals(prefix)) {
1523                                String v = _valueOrNull(k);
1524                                if (v != null) {
1525                                        String _k = k.substring(prefix.length());
1526                                        m.put(_k, v);
1527                                }
1528                        }
1529                }
1530                return m;
1531        }
1532
1533}
1534
1535interface ListLogProperties extends LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
1536
1537        @Override
1538        default @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1539                for (var props : properties()) {
1540                        var value = props.valueOrNull(key);
1541                        if (value != null) {
1542                                return value;
1543                        }
1544                }
1545                return null;
1546        }
1547
1548        @Override
1549        default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key,
1550                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor) {
1551                for (var props : properties()) {
1552                        var value = props.visit(key, visitor);
1553                        if (value != null) {
1554                                return value;
1555                        }
1556                }
1557                return null;
1558        }
1559
1560        @Override
1561        default String description(String key) {
1562                var descriptions = new ArrayList<String>();
1563                visit(key, (source, sourceKey) -> {
1564                        descriptions.add(source.description(sourceKey));
1565                        return null;
1566                });
1567                String description = String.join(", ", descriptions);
1568                if (description.length() > 120) {
1569                        return "\n    " + String.join(",\n    ", descriptions);
1570                }
1571                return description;
1572        }
1573
1574        LogProperties[] properties();
1575
1576        default StringBuilder toString(StringBuilder sb) {
1577                sb.append(getClass().getSimpleName());
1578                sb.append("[properties=").append(Arrays.deepToString(properties())).append("]");
1579                return sb;
1580        }
1581
1582        /*
1583         * Reports components separated by commas without the error description's line
1584         * wrapping (via LogPropertiesReporting.describe, the same fallback chain
1585         * LogReporter#appendGlobalProperties uses for the top level LogProperties a LogConfig
1586         * was built with) rather than per key.
1587         */
1588        @Override
1589        default void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
1590                boolean first = true;
1591                for (var p : properties()) {
1592                        if (first) {
1593                                first = false;
1594                        }
1595                        else {
1596                                out.append(", ");
1597                        }
1598                        LogPropertiesReporting.describe(out, p);
1599                }
1600        }
1601
1602}
1603
1604/*
1605 * Shared by ListLogProperties#report(Appendable) (recursively, per component) and
1606 * LogReporter's own appendGlobalProperties(Appendable, LogProperties) (for the top level
1607 * LogProperties a LogConfig was built with), so there is exactly one fallback chain for
1608 * "how do we describe an arbitrary LogProperties for a report": an explicit
1609 * Reportable#report(...) if implemented, else the concrete class' fully qualified name
1610 * (stable and free: no override needed), else, only for the rare case where the FQCN
1611 * itself is null (e.g. one of StandardProperties' own per constant enum bodies, which are
1612 * anonymous classes under the hood, before it implemented Reportable directly),
1613 * description(key) with a dummy key, since that is the only description() such a
1614 * LogProperties is guaranteed to answer at all.
1615 */
1616final class LogPropertiesReporting {
1617
1618        static final String DESCRIBE_KEY = "logging.reporter.describe";
1619
1620        private LogPropertiesReporting() {
1621        }
1622
1623        static void describe(Appendable out, LogProperties properties) throws IOException {
1624                if (properties instanceof LogReporter.Reportable r) {
1625                        r.report(out);
1626                        return;
1627                }
1628                String fqcn = properties.getClass().getCanonicalName();
1629                if (fqcn != null) {
1630                        out.append(fqcn);
1631                        return;
1632                }
1633                out.append(properties.description(DESCRIBE_KEY));
1634        }
1635
1636}

1638@SuppressWarnings("ArrayRecordComponent") // TODO we did this originall because it was hot
1639                                                                                        // path but not anymore
1640record CompositeMutableLogProperties(LogProperties[] properties) implements ListLogProperties, MutableLogProperties {
1641
1642        @Override
1643        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality") // identity check to avoid self-recursion if a
1644                                                                                        // composite contains itself
1645        public MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value) {
1646                for (var p : properties()) {
1647                        if (p instanceof MutableLogProperties mp && mp != this) {
1648                                mp.put(key, value);
1649                                return this;
1650                        }
1651                }
1652                return this;
1653        }
1654
1655        @Override
1656        public String toString() {
1657                return toString(new StringBuilder()).toString();
1658        }
1659
1660}

1663                                                                                        // path but not anymore
